findings.text: follow-on: the probe scripts named in the fragment's command lines (list_probe.py at :35, data_probe.py at :58 and dbsel_plain.py at :88) were written under /tmp and never committed, so the investigation cannot be re-run from the committed artifact; the raw receipts survive only in the run directory, which a retention sweep reclaims. Committing the three small probe scripts beside the fragment would make the evidence regenerable.

follow-on: retry_failures lists three ids (dbsel-strace-preflight, dbsel-selene-eof, dbsel-output-symlink) but failure_attribution fixes a cause for only two; dbsel-selene-eof carries none. That eof was the first scratch run's expected missing-EQSLE.DATA iteration (dbsel-plain.log STDERR 'end-of-file during read, unit 7 ... EQSLE.DATA'), not a scaffolding fault, so recording it as an unattributed retry id makes the stop-rule count ambiguous for a reader.

follow-on: the remote probes implement the facility hop inline (ssh -T -F ~/.ssh/config jt-60sa ... python3 - < probe.py) instead of the repository's canonical remote-execution owner imas_codex/remote/executor.py:1071 run_python_script with a script under imas_codex/remote/scripts/; jt-60sa is a configured facility (imas_codex/config/facilities/jt-60sa.yaml, ssh_host: jt-60sa), so the hop is a capability the repository already owns.

Docked because the probe scripts named in the fragment's own command lines (list_probe.py at :35, data_probe.py at :58, dbsel_plain.py at :88) were staged under /tmp and never committed, so the investigation cannot be re-run from the record and the raw receipts survive only in the run directory, which crew gc reclaims.
justifications.evidence: I reconciled the fragment's numbers against the run's own logs and they match: fledd-lists.log carries all 42 eqlist_get_rev_ records (IRET/NLIST/TIMES) whose values reproduce fledd-equilibrium-read.html:41-50 exactly, and fledd-data.log carries the four psi SHA-256 digests and MIN/MAX ranges matching :65-73. The worker supplies positive controls (nonempty time lists; FINITE=True and nonconstant grids) so the zero counts are not read from empty output, and it preserves the nonfatal ERROR(EQEXTRA) RETURN CODE = 991 and states that the DBSEL wrapper exit alone is insufficient, citing SELENE's own registration success and iret=0.
justifications.fit: The fragment follows the docs/evidence/fragments convention and names only mechanisms; commit 24346b9's subject docs(equilibrium): record socket reads and DBSEL isolation is conventional and carries a body, and no plan, sprint, ticket or gate identifier appears in the fragment text; the fragment uses no plan-label vocabulary.
justifications.goal_fidelity: §49's goal is investigation-only: record the FLEDD socket and DBSEL equilibrium routes and the meaning of the nonzero return codes. The fragment docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-discovery-completion/fledd-equilibrium-read.html:11-31 gives operational meanings for 6415 (no time list on IDs 1-4 for that shot) and 6151 (IDs 5-8 empty in every shot), :33-73 records four full 129x129 psi grids for FAME and EQDB, and :75-108 records DBSEL's inputs, outputs and scratch-local invocation. Docked because deliverable (a) asks the codes be decoded from the eqdbms source, which this account cannot read: source-codes.log shows ls on eqdbms/S exits 2 with Permission denied, so the source-level names are correctly left as a facility follow-on rather than asserted.
justifications.reuse: No production code was added, so the landed change forks no repository capability. Docked because the remote probes ran inline (fledd-equilibrium-read.html:35,58,88 show ssh -T -F ~/.ssh/config jt-60sa ... python3 - < probe.py) rather than through the repository's own remote-execution owner, imas_codex/remote/executor.py:1071 run_python_script, which I confirmed exists; the facility hop is thereby implemented outside the owner the repo names as canonical.
